text:
anya: Quick follow-up from the slab rewrite RFC — diving into fragmentation "fracture" mitigation and how the evictor should surface pages for CPU/NVMe fallbacks. TL;DR: i'm proposing two small orthogonal changes: 1) a lightweight per-tenant frag-score bloom to mark sticky subpages, and 2) an evictor -> runtime 'reconcile' API so we can signal low-cost defrag attempts before full offload. thoughts on tradeoffs/compat/back-compat?

zane: Do we have a cost model for scanning vs moving? frag-score only helps if moving wins often.

sam: +1 on cost model. We should capture tokens-per-move (latency/cost) and recent reuse window. otherwise scanner will thrash.

may: For API shape, something tiny might work:
```
reconcile_eviction(tenant_id, page_range, urgency="low") -> {moved: int, scanned: int}
```
returns quick metrics and a best-effort flag. keep it sync so caller can choose to retry later.

liam: Backwards compat: default behavior must be no-op if runtime doesn't implement reconcile. Evictor falls back to current offload path. That keeps existing contracts.

harper: Concern: defrag attempts on hot paths could add tail latency. We should bound time spent per request and surface SLO-safe creds (e.g., urgent vs background).

anya: Agreed. idea: reconcile API has an 'urgency' and 'budget_ms' param; evictor only calls when it has spare headroom (or async worker). Also frag-score should bias candidates for cheap local compacts (within slab) before moving pages.

zane: How do we build frag-score cheaply? Per-subpage counters + decaying EWMA? or sampling-based bloom? We need something fast and low-mem.

sam: Sampling looks promising: piggyback on allocation/free events and sample 1/256 ops to increment counters. keep counters uint8 and decay periodically. cheap and low overhead.

may: Implementation note: tie frag-score to allocation view so we can prefer coalescing within same arena. For multi-tenant fairness, expose tenant-weighted thresholds.

liam: Also, reconcile should be idempotent and cancellable. If runtime evicts the pages during reconcile, we should abort. add a request-id and a cancel endpoint.

anya: Good call. propose: reconcile returns a token and a short-lived cancellation endpoint. default budget_ms=5ms for sync, >50ms goes to async queue.

harper: We need telemetry hooks: moved/scanned per tenant, budget vs actual, latency P99. If we don't track it, we'll regret it after rollout.

jess: I can run a quick bench: microbench that simulates small alloc/dealloc churn and tries reconcile with budgets [1,5,20ms] and compares evict->offload vs reconcile-first. will post numbers.

anya: Awesome. For rollout plan: implement reconcile shim that is opt-in via config flag, default off. Stage: local tests -> perf bench -> staged canary on Dedicated -> enable for customers after metrics look good.

zane: One more tradeoff: moving pages to coalesce increases short-term memory usage. Need admission control tied to tenant quotas. Otherwise one tenant could blow host memory defragging.

sam: Agreed. reconcile should consult current free-headroom and tenant quota; if headroom < threshold, reconcile should skip.

may: Pseudocode sketch for reconcile decision: 
```
if frag_score(range) < THRESH: return SKIP
if tenant_quota_available() < MIN_HEADROOM: return DEFER
run_compact(range, budget_ms)
```
Return metrics so caller can adapt.

liam: API ergonomics: SDK-level helper that retries reconcile with backoff then falls back to offload when reconcile returns SKIP/DEFER. keeps caller simple.

anya: Sounds like consensus. Action items: jess -> bench (this week). may -> small API PR + proto types. zane/sam -> cost model sketch and thresholds. harper -> telemetry metrics list. i'll draft a brief RFC addendum capturing API shape, budget semantics, and rollout.

ops-bot: Reminder: eng-runtime sync in 2h — we can discuss the addendum then. :bell:

jess: Will post bench results in thread when ready.

anya: Thanks all — keeping the reconcile opt-in and budgeted should let us get fragmentation wins without surprising cost spikes.
